note: One idea today. Our workers may carry a hidden start-up load (skills list, memory, MCP) on every run. `--bare` would remove it but does not work on the subscription. Cheaper switches do exist. First step: one free measurement on your PC; only then change code.

questions: Which flags or env vars we can use today cut the per-run start-up load without losing our tools?
Is the start-up load big enough to matter next to a Vera run ($0.06) or a Sage run ($0.15)?
gaps: No official number for the start-up load of `claude -p --system-prompt` on a PC with skills; only user reports (about 12K to 72K tokens, different versions).
No official source on whether `--disable-slash-commands` removes the skills list in `-p` today (a May 2026 bug report says it did not; it is marked closed, fix version unknown).
Could not read the official memory page for exact CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY wording; only mirrors.
No YouTube policy change found for November 2026 (latest coverage is the July 2026 clarification).

Claude Code 2.1.330: `claude -p` exits 1 when output goes to a full disk; subagent progress summaries use far fewer tokens.
Claude Code 2.1.328/2.1.331: better prompt caching for Code Mode with MCP; `--resume` in another permission mode kept cache. Not used by our one-shot workers.

Docs: bare mode 'will become the default for -p in a future release'. It needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and never reads OAuth. Watch this: when it becomes default, subscription workers could break or silently need a key.

ideas.title: Measure the hidden start-up load of our workers, then switch off what they don't need
ideas.problem: workers.py run() starts every worker as `claude -p --no-session-persistence --system-prompt ... --tools ...` in ~/Agent-HQ-workers/<agent>/ using the owner's normal Claude Code setup. A replaced system prompt does not stop Claude Code from adding the skills list (the owner has user skills such as senior-ui-ux), user memory, plugins and MCP tool names. Docs: 'Every skill in the skill listing adds to your context on every turn' (A, skills doc). A user measured ~12K injected tokens per call even with --system-prompt (C, issue #60251). Vera costs ~$0.06 and a short Sage ~$0.15 (CLAUDE.md), so a fixed ~12K cache write (1h write $4/M = ~$0.05) could be a third or more of a short run. We have never measured it: `usage` stores tokens, but nobody has looked at a run with no real task. `--bare` would remove all of it but cannot be used: docs say it 'never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain', and the workers run on the subscription.
ideas.proposal: Step 1 (free, 10 min, no code): in ~/Agent-HQ-workers/vera run `claude -p "Reply OK" --output-format json --no-session-persistence --system-prompt "Reply OK" --tools ""` and read usage.cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens. Repeat with `--disable-slash-commands --strict-mcp-config` and with env CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1. If the plain run is under ~3K tokens, STOP: nothing to gain, drop the idea. Step 2 (only if the load is >=8K): in workers.run() (workers.py line ~87) add those two flags and the env var to `cmd`/env, behind a new rule `workers.lean_start` (rules.py, default off, scope: Doulya/Sage/Vera/Serge/Calina/Israa, NOT Atlas, who needs his memory and skills). workers.py is protected from Ghassan, so the Builder chat does it. Step 3: record input+cache tokens of the first request per agent in the existing `usage` rows (already there: input_tokens, cache_tokens) and compare 5 runs on vs off.
ideas.gain: Unknown until step 1. If the load is ~12K tokens: about $0.05 less API-value per run, or roughly 30-50% of a Vera run and 10-30% of a Sage run, which also stretches SUBSCRIPTION_DAILY_VALUE_USD allowances (Sage 6.00, Calina 6.00). Measure: median (input+cache_tokens) of the first turn per agent before/after, from the usage table.
ideas.test: Normal: Vera runs a verdict with lean_start on; structured_output still arrives and the verdict matches the run with it off on the same idea. Edge: Calina with WebSearch/WebFetch and a JSON schema still returns structured_output (the tools she needs must not be removed by --strict-mcp-config; she uses built-in tools, not MCP). Failure: if a flag is unknown on the owner's installed Claude Code (older app copy) the run must fall back to the old command, not raise Unavailable. Pass = same answers on 3 test ideas, first-turn tokens down by the step-1 amount, zero new Unavailable events in 5 days.
ideas.confidence_why: Docs (A) prove the skills list costs tokens every turn and that --bare is unusable on the subscription. The size on the owner's PC rests on one user report (C, closed bug, fix version unknown). That is why step 1 is a measurement, not a change.
ideas.risks: --disable-slash-commands may still ship the skills list in some versions (issue #60251), so the flag could do nothing: step 1 shows it. Turning memory off for workers changes nothing they rely on (they have no memory files; Atlas is excluded). When docs make --bare the default for -p ('in a future release'), subscription workers could stop authenticating: re-check the changelog daily; this is a separate warning item. No outside code is installed.
